name: Simeon
overview: Simeon is a male biblical figure known as a prophet and teacher in Antioch, as noted in Acts 13:1. While his tribal affiliation is not specified in this context, his role in the early church highlights his spiritual leadership. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him in this reference.
namesAndTitles: The name Simeon means 'he has heard,' reflecting a Hebrew origin and possibly indicating a character attentive to God's voice. Another name associated with him is Niger, though its meaning is not provided. Both names appear in Acts 13:1, showing the dual identification of this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for this Simeon beyond what is listed in his role as a prophet and teacher in Antioch. No further familial connections are provided in the available information.
scriptureSignificance: Simeon is significant in the New Testament as a prophetic leader within the early church at Antioch, contributing to the foundation of Christian teaching and mission. This role contrasts with the earlier Simeon, the son of Jacob, whose descendants were known for their fierceness and eventual integration into the tribe of Judah. The New Testament Simeon's ministry demonstrates the continuation of God's work through faithful servants in the church.
